description: Starbucks launched its 'Race Together' campaign asking baristas to write the phrase on cups and discuss race with customers.
reaction: Widespread mockery and criticism on social media; the company's communications chief temporarily deleted his Twitter account and the cup-writing phase was ended within a week.
business_impact: campaign ended after one week, no lasting impact

description: The US EPA issued a notice of violation revealing Volkswagen had installed software to cheat diesel emissions tests on roughly 500,000 US vehicles.
reaction: Public outrage, class-action suits, congressional hearings and criminal probes; the CEO resigned within a week and US diesel sales were halted.
business_impact: CEO resigned, more than $25 billion in US penalties and buybacks

description: Turing, led by CEO Martin Shkreli, raised the price of the decades-old drug Daraprim from $13.50 to $750 per pill.
reaction: Viral outrage on social media, condemnation from presidential candidates and physician groups, and congressional hearings; Shkreli became a national symbol of drug-price anger.
business_impact: congressional hearings; price partially rolled back for hospitals

description: Chipotle closed 43 restaurants in Washington and Oregon after an E. coli outbreak, the first of several foodborne illness clusters linked to the chain in late 2015.
reaction: Sustained national coverage, customer avoidance, a federal criminal investigation and shareholder suits.
business_impact: same-store sales down about 30% in December 2015, stock fell roughly 40% over following months

description: Starbucks released a plain red holiday cup without seasonal imagery, which a viral video framed as part of a 'war on Christmas'.
reaction: Viral social media debate, calls to boycott from some Christian customers, and comments from presidential candidate Donald Trump.
business_impact: no measurable impact

description: Target publicly affirmed that transgender customers and employees could use the bathroom matching their gender identity.
reaction: The American Family Association launched a boycott pledge that gathered more than 1 million signatures and protests occurred in stores.
business_impact: traffic declined for several quarters; $20 million spent adding single-stall bathrooms

description: Reports highlighted that Mylan had raised the list price of a two-pack of EpiPens from about $100 to more than $600 since 2007.
reaction: Viral parent outrage, letters from senators, and a House Oversight hearing in September where CEO Heather Bresch was grilled.
business_impact: congressional hearing; generic version launched; $465 million Medicaid settlement

description: Regulators fined Wells Fargo $185 million for employees opening roughly 2 million unauthorized customer accounts to meet sales targets.
reaction: Public anger, Senate and House hearings where CEO John Stumpf was berated, and calls for his resignation.
business_impact: CEO resigned October 2016; Fed asset cap; billions in fines

description: A New Balance executive told the Wall Street Journal that the Trump administration would move trade policy 'in the right direction'.
reaction: Customers posted videos burning or trashing New Balance shoes, while a white-supremacist blog praised the brand, prompting the company to disavow it.
business_impact: apology/clarification, no lasting impact

description: Grubhub CEO Matt Maloney emailed employees after the election saying those who agreed with Donald Trump's rhetoric should resign.
reaction: #BoycottGrubhub trended among Trump supporters and the stock dipped; Maloney issued a clarification.
business_impact: clarification issued, stock dip, no lasting impact

description: Kellogg's pulled its advertising from Breitbart News, saying the site did not align with its values.
reaction: Breitbart launched a #DumpKelloggs boycott petition that gathered hundreds of thousands of signatures.
business_impact: no measurable impact

description: Uber turned off surge pricing at JFK during a taxi strike protesting the travel ban, and its CEO sat on a Trump business council.
reaction: #DeleteUber went viral and about 200,000 users deleted their accounts; Lyft surged in app rankings and CEO Kalanick quit the council days later.
business_impact: 200,000 account deletions; CEO left presidential advisory council

description: Nordstrom dropped Ivanka Trump's clothing line, citing declining sales, amid the #GrabYourWallet campaign.
reaction: President Trump attacked the retailer on Twitter, his supporters called for a boycott, and the stock briefly fell.
business_impact: brief stock dip, no lasting impact

description: Former engineer Susan Fowler published a blog post describing systemic sexual harassment and HR failures at Uber.
reaction: Viral outrage, an internal investigation led by Eric Holder, further scandals, and investor pressure that forced CEO Travis Kalanick to resign in June 2017.
business_impact: CEO resigned June 2017; 20 employees fired

description: Pepsi released an ad in which Kendall Jenner defuses a protest by handing a police officer a Pepsi.
reaction: Widespread ridicule and accusations of trivializing protest movements; Pepsi pulled the ad and apologized within 24 hours.
business_impact: ad pulled, apology, no lasting impact

description: Video showed passenger David Dao being forcibly dragged off an overbooked United Express flight in Chicago.
reaction: Global viral outrage, boycott calls, congressional hearings and a widely criticized CEO response; the stock lost about $1 billion in value at one point.
business_impact: settlement with passenger; policy changes; CEO lost planned chairmanship

description: Equifax disclosed a breach exposing personal data of about 147 million Americans, weeks after discovering it.
reaction: Public fury over the delayed disclosure and executive stock sales, congressional hearings, and dozens of lawsuits.
business_impact: CEO retired September 26, 2017; $700 million settlement

description: Founder-CEO John Schnatter blamed NFL player protests during the national anthem for weak pizza sales on an earnings call.
reaction: Backlash from fans and players, praise from a neo-Nazi site that the company disavowed, and a stock slide; the company apologized two weeks later and Schnatter stepped down as CEO in December.
business_impact: CEO stepped down December 2017; stock fell about 13%

description: Keurig pulled its advertising from Sean Hannity's Fox News show after his coverage of the Roy Moore allegations.
reaction: Hannity supporters posted videos smashing Keurig machines; the CEO apologized internally for taking sides.
business_impact: CEO apology, no lasting impact

description: H&M's website showed a Black child modeling a hoodie reading 'Coolest Monkey in the Jungle'.
reaction: Viral outrage, The Weeknd and G-Eazy ended partnerships, and the company apologized and hired a diversity leader.
business_impact: celebrity partnerships ended, apology

description: Delta ended a group travel discount for NRA members after the Parkland shooting.
reaction: Gun-rights supporters called for a boycott and Georgia lawmakers stripped a $40 million jet-fuel tax break from pending legislation.
business_impact: lost $40 million state tax break (later restored)

description: Dick's announced it would stop selling assault-style rifles and raise the gun-buying age to 21 after the Parkland shooting.
reaction: Boycott calls from gun-rights groups and praise from gun-control advocates; the company later destroyed its rifle inventory.
business_impact: company estimated about $250 million in lost hunting sales

description: The New York Times and Observer reported that Cambridge Analytica had harvested data on up to 87 million Facebook users without consent.
reaction: #DeleteFacebook trended, the stock lost more than $100 billion in value within days, and Mark Zuckerberg testified before Congress in April.
business_impact: $5 billion FTC fine (2019); congressional testimony; sustained reputational damage

description: Video spread of two Black men being arrested at a Philadelphia Starbucks after a manager called police while they waited for a business associate.
reaction: Protests inside the store, #BoycottStarbucks trended, and the company closed 8,000 US stores for an afternoon of racial-bias training on May 29.
business_impact: 8,000 stores closed for training (estimated $12 million in lost sales); policy changes

description: Forbes reported that founder John Schnatter used a racial slur during a media-training conference call in May.
reaction: Immediate public outcry; Schnatter resigned as chairman the same day, his image was removed from marketing, and sponsors and universities cut ties.
business_impact: founder resigned as chairman; sales declines through 2018-2019

description: Nike made Colin Kaepernick the face of its 30th-anniversary 'Just Do It' campaign.
reaction: #NikeBoycott trended and some customers burned Nike gear, while supporters rallied; the stock dipped briefly then hit a record high within two weeks.
business_impact: online sales up 31% in following days; stock at all-time high within two weeks

description: Amazon announced it would locate half of its HQ2 in Long Island City, New York, in exchange for roughly $3 billion in incentives.
reaction: Sustained protests from local politicians, unions and residents over subsidies and housing; Amazon cancelled the New York plan on February 14, 2019.
business_impact: New York HQ2 plan cancelled

description: Reuters reported that J&J had known for decades that its talc baby powder sometimes tested positive for asbestos.
reaction: Public outrage and a flood of lawsuits; the stock fell 10% in a day, wiping out about $40 billion in market value.
business_impact: stock down 10% in one day; talc baby powder discontinued in North America in 2020; billions in litigation

description: Gillette released 'The Best Men Can Be', an ad addressing toxic masculinity in the wake of #MeToo.
reaction: The ad became one of YouTube's most-disliked videos amid boycott calls from critics who felt lectured, while others praised it.
business_impact: no measurable sales impact

description: The FAA grounded the 737 MAX after the Ethiopian Airlines crash, the second fatal MAX crash in five months, amid revelations about the MCAS flight-control system.
reaction: Global outrage, victim-family campaigns, congressional hearings exposing internal messages, and public distrust of the aircraft.
business_impact: CEO Dennis Muilenburg fired December 2019; 20-month grounding; more than $20 billion in costs

description: Wayfair employees learned the company had sold about $200,000 of beds to a contractor operating a migrant child detention facility in Texas.
reaction: More than 500 employees staged a walkout in Boston and #BoycottWayfair trended; the company donated $100,000 to the Red Cross.
business_impact: employee walkout, donation, no lasting impact

description: Capital One disclosed a breach exposing data of about 106 million US and Canadian credit card customers and applicants.
reaction: Public anger, class-action suits, and Senate Banking Committee demands for consumer protections.
business_impact: $80 million OCC penalty; $190 million class settlement

description: Reports revealed that Stephen Ross, owner of Equinox and SoulCycle's parent, was hosting a high-dollar fundraiser for President Trump.
reaction: Celebrities and customers called for boycotts and cancelled memberships; the brands issued statements distancing themselves from Ross.
business_impact: membership cancellations, no lasting impact reported

description: Amid an FDA warning letter over youth marketing, a federal probe and a wave of vaping-related illnesses, Juul's CEO stepped down and the company halted all US advertising.
reaction: Sustained public anger from parents, school districts and lawmakers over teen vaping, with state lawsuits, a congressional investigation and flavor bans.
business_impact: CEO replaced; advertising halted; flavored pods pulled; billions in settlements

description: Rockets GM Daryl Morey tweeted support for Hong Kong protesters, and the NBA's initial statement calling it 'regrettable' drew bipartisan criticism in the US.
reaction: US politicians from both parties accused the league of bowing to China while Chinese partners suspended ties; fans protested at games.
business_impact: NBA estimated hundreds of millions in lost China revenue

description: Chick-fil-A said it would stop donating to the Salvation Army and Fellowship of Christian Athletes after years of LGBTQ-related criticism.
reaction: Conservative leaders accused the chain of betrayal and 49 signed a letter urging it to reverse course, while LGBTQ groups remained skeptical.
business_impact: no measurable impact

description: Peloton's holiday ad showed a husband giving his already-fit wife an exercise bike, which viewers widely mocked as sexist and dystopian.
reaction: Viral ridicule and parodies; the stock fell about 9% in one day, erasing roughly $942 million in market value.
business_impact: stock down 9% in one day, no lasting impact

description: Amazon fired Staten Island warehouse worker Chris Smalls hours after he led a walkout over COVID-19 safety conditions.
reaction: The New York attorney general called the firing disgraceful, a leaked memo disparaging Smalls fueled outrage, and senators demanded answers.
business_impact: NY AG lawsuit; VP Tim Bray resigned in protest; unionization drive followed

description: As pandemic use exploded, Zoom faced revelations about 'Zoombombing', misleading encryption claims and data sharing with Facebook.
reaction: Schools and companies banned the app, the New York attorney general and FBI issued warnings, and the FTC later brought a complaint; Zoom announced a 90-day security freeze.
business_impact: FTC settlement (2020); $85 million class settlement

description: CrossFit CEO Greg Glassman tweeted 'It's FLOYD-19' in response to a post calling racism a public health issue.
reaction: Reebok and other sponsors cut ties, more than 1,000 affiliated gyms disaffiliated, and Glassman resigned within days and sold the company.
business_impact: CEO resigned; founder sold company; sponsor exits

description: Civil rights groups launched the #StopHateForProfit campaign urging advertisers to pause Facebook spending over its handling of hate speech and misinformation.
reaction: More than 1,000 advertisers including Unilever, Coca-Cola and Starbucks paused ads in July; the stock fell 8% in a day.
business_impact: stock fell 8% on June 26; revenue impact minimal

description: Goya CEO Robert Unanue praised President Trump at a White House event, saying the country was 'truly blessed' to have him as a leader.
reaction: #Goyaway and #BoycottGoya trended with calls from Latino politicians and celebrities, while supporters organized a 'buycott' that boosted sales.
business_impact: sales rose on counter-boycott; no lasting negative impact

description: A leaked training slide listed MAGA attire as unacceptable at work while permitting BLM and LGBTQ messaging.
reaction: President Trump tweeted 'Don't buy GOODYEAR TIRES' and supporters called for a boycott; the stock fell and the company clarified its policy.
business_impact: stock dipped about 6%, no lasting impact

description: Netflix released the French film 'Cuties', which critics accused of sexualizing children, after an earlier poster controversy.
reaction: #CancelNetflix trended, cancellations spiked, senators demanded a DOJ review, and a Texas grand jury indicted Netflix.
business_impact: cancellation rate spiked several-fold for days; Texas indictment (later dismissed)

description: Bed Bath & Beyond, Kohl's and other retailers dropped MyPillow after CEO Mike Lindell promoted election-fraud claims following the January 6 attack.
reaction: Lindell supporters called for boycotts of the retailers while critics pressured remaining sellers to follow; Lindell said the company lost major retail distribution.
business_impact: MyPillow lost major retail accounts

description: Robinhood restricted buying of GameStop and other 'meme stocks' at the peak of the retail trading frenzy.
reaction: Users flooded app stores with one-star reviews, class actions were filed within hours, politicians from AOC to Ted Cruz condemned the move, and Congress held hearings.
business_impact: congressional hearing; $70 million FINRA penalty; reputational damage ahead of IPO

description: Delta's and Coca-Cola's CEOs publicly criticized Georgia's new voting law as unacceptable.
reaction: Republican leaders including Donald Trump urged boycotts of both companies and the Georgia House voted to strip Delta's jet-fuel tax break.
business_impact: Georgia House vote to repeal tax break (did not pass Senate); no measurable sales impact

description: MLB moved the 2021 All-Star Game out of Atlanta in response to Georgia's voting law.
reaction: Trump and Republican officials called for a boycott of baseball and its sponsors, while Georgia's governor denounced 'cancel culture'; supporters praised the move.
business_impact: Atlanta lost an estimated $100 million in tourism; no measurable MLB impact

description: The CPSC warned families to stop using the Peloton Tread+ after a child's death and dozens of injuries, and Peloton publicly rejected the warning as inaccurate.
reaction: Widespread criticism of the company's defiance from safety advocates, parents and lawmakers; Peloton reversed course and recalled 125,000 treadmills on May 5.
business_impact: full recall; $19 million CPSC civil penalty (2023); stock decline

description: California's civil rights agency sued Activision Blizzard alleging a 'frat boy' culture of sexual harassment and pay discrimination.
reaction: Employees staged walkouts, more than 2,000 signed a letter condemning management's response, and a November WSJ report on CEO Bobby Kotick's knowledge brought calls for his resignation.
business_impact: SEC and EEOC settlements; executive departures; Microsoft acquisition followed

description: Whistleblower Frances Haugen revealed herself on 60 Minutes after leaking internal research showing Facebook knew Instagram harmed teen mental health.
reaction: Bipartisan Senate hearing on October 5, global coverage of the 'Facebook Files', and renewed calls for regulation and breakup.
business_impact: congressional hearings; company renamed Meta weeks later; state AG lawsuits

description: A crowd crush at the Live Nation-promoted Astroworld Festival in Houston killed 10 people during Travis Scott's set.
reaction: National outrage over crowd management, hundreds of lawsuits naming Live Nation, and a congressional inquiry into the promoter's safety practices.
business_impact: hundreds of lawsuits (settled); congressional inquiry

description: A video spread of Better.com CEO Vishal Garg laying off about 900 employees in a brief Zoom call days before the holidays.
reaction: Viral condemnation of the callous delivery; three top executives resigned and Garg took a leave of absence.
business_impact: CEO took leave; three executives resigned

description: Spotify removed Neil Young's catalog after he demanded it choose between his music and Joe Rogan's podcast over COVID misinformation.
reaction: #DeleteSpotify trended, other artists pulled music, and the stock fell sharply; Spotify added content advisories and Rogan apologized.
business_impact: stock lost about $2 billion in a day and fell roughly 25% in two weeks

description: Disney CEO Bob Chapek, after criticism from employees for silence, publicly opposed Florida's Parental Rights in Education bill and paused state political donations.
reaction: Employees walked out over the initial silence, then Governor DeSantis and conservatives attacked the company, and the legislature dissolved Disney's special district in April.
business_impact: Reedy Creek district dissolved; multi-year legal fight; contributed to CEO Chapek's ouster in November 2022

description: A nationwide infant formula shortage, triggered by Abbott's February recall and the shutdown of its Sturgis plant after contamination findings, became a national crisis.
reaction: Parents' anger dominated news coverage, lawmakers demanded answers, and Abbott's CEO apologized at a House hearing on May 25.
business_impact: plant shut for months; consent decree; congressional hearings; market share loss

description: Days after Elon Musk's takeover, Twitter laid off roughly half its 7,500 employees by email, amid chaotic verification changes.
reaction: Lawsuits over WARN Act notice, public anger at the handling, and major advertisers including General Mills and Pfizer paused spending.
business_impact: advertiser exodus; ad revenue reportedly halved within months

description: Ticketmaster's Taylor Swift Eras Tour presale crashed under demand and the general sale was cancelled, leaving millions of fans without tickets.
reaction: Fan fury went viral, Swift criticized the company, lawmakers from both parties attacked Live Nation's market power, and the Senate held a hearing in January 2023.
business_impact: Senate hearing; contributed to 2024 DOJ antitrust lawsuit

description: Balenciaga ran a campaign showing children holding teddy bears in bondage-style harnesses, alongside a second campaign featuring documents from a child-pornography court case.
reaction: Viral US outrage and boycott calls, Kim Kardashian said she was 're-evaluating' her partnership, and the brand apologized and sued its production company.
business_impact: campaign pulled, apologies, reported sales slump in following months

description: Southwest's scheduling systems collapsed during a winter storm, cancelling nearly 17,000 flights over the holidays while other airlines recovered.
reaction: Stranded passengers' stories dominated news for a week, the Transportation Secretary and senators demanded accountability, and a Senate hearing followed.
business_impact: $140 million DOT penalty; more than $1 billion in costs

description: With egg prices up more than 100% year over year, the largest US egg producer reported record profits and farm groups accused the industry of price gouging.
reaction: Viral consumer anger over egg prices, a Farm Action letter to the FTC, and senators demanding an investigation.
business_impact: calls for FTC probe; prices fell by spring

description: After its February 3 derailment and controlled burn of vinyl chloride in East Palestine, Ohio, Norfolk Southern faced accusations of negligence and inadequate response.
reaction: Residents' anger at a town hall the CEO skipped, viral images of dead fish and black smoke, bipartisan condemnation, and a Senate hearing on March 9.
business_impact: $600 million class settlement; more than $1 billion in costs; rail-safety legislation push

description: Bud Light sent a personalized can to transgender influencer Dylan Mulvaney, who posted about it on Instagram.
reaction: Conservative celebrities and customers launched a boycott, Kid Rock shot cases of beer on video, and LGBTQ groups later criticized the company's retreat.
business_impact: US sales down 25-30% for months; lost top-selling beer status; marketing executives placed on leave

description: Target pulled some Pride Month merchandise after confrontations in stores and threats to employees.
reaction: Conservative boycott calls over the collection were followed by criticism from LGBTQ groups for capitulating; the company cited the backlash for a sales decline.
business_impact: Q2 comparable sales down 5.4%; roughly $10 billion in market value lost

description: As the search for OceanGate's Titan submersible unfolded, reports emerged that CEO Stockton Rush had dismissed repeated safety warnings about the vessel.
reaction: Intense global attention and public anger at the company's safety culture after the implosion was confirmed; Coast Guard investigation and lawsuits followed.
business_impact: company suspended operations; Coast Guard inquiry; wrongful death suits

description: Disney CEO Bob Iger told CNBC that striking writers' and actors' demands were 'not realistic' and 'disturbing'.
reaction: Union leaders and actors denounced the comments as out of touch given his pay, and the clip became a rallying point for the Hollywood strikes.
business_impact: reputational; no direct financial impact

description: A lawsuit alleged Panera's highly caffeinated Charged Lemonade caused the death of a 21-year-old college student with a heart condition.
reaction: Viral coverage of the drink's caffeine content and additional wrongful-death suits; Panera added warnings and discontinued the drink in May 2024.
business_impact: product discontinued; lawsuits settled

description: Elon Musk replied 'You have said the actual truth' to a post echoing an antisemitic conspiracy theory, days after a Media Matters report on ads next to extremist content.
reaction: IBM, Apple, Disney, Comcast and other major advertisers paused spending on X, and the White House condemned the post.
business_impact: major advertiser exodus; X reportedly lost tens of millions in Q4 ad revenue

description: A door plug blew out of a Boeing 737 MAX 9 on Alaska Airlines Flight 1282, leading the FAA to ground the fleet and exposing quality-control failures.
reaction: Intense public and media scrutiny, whistleblower revelations, Senate hearings and viral distrust of Boeing aircraft through the spring.
business_impact: CEO Dave Calhoun announced departure March 25, 2024; FAA production cap; DOJ criminal case revived; stock down 30%+

description: Google's Gemini AI generated historically inaccurate images, such as racially diverse Nazi soldiers and US founding fathers, and refused some prompts.
reaction: Viral ridicule and accusations of 'woke' bias, Google paused people-image generation on February 22, and CEO Sundar Pichai called the failures 'unacceptable' as the stock fell.
business_impact: feature paused; stock fell about 4%; internal reorganization

description: Kellogg CEO Gary Pilnick suggested on CNBC that cash-strapped families eat 'cereal for dinner' as food prices rose.
reaction: The clip went viral as tone-deaf, TikTok users called for a Kellogg's boycott, and the comment became a symbol of grocery-price anger.
business_impact: boycott calls, no measurable impact

description: Reports that Wendy's planned to test 'dynamic pricing' on digital menu boards in 2025 were widely read as Uber-style surge pricing for burgers.
reaction: Viral outrage from customers and politicians including Senator Warren, rivals trolled the chain, and Wendy's issued a statement denying it would raise prices at busy times.
business_impact: clarification issued, plan reframed, no lasting impact

description: Sonos released a redesigned app on May 7, 2024 that removed core features and broke functionality for many users of its speakers.
reaction: Months of furious customer complaints, a public CEO apology, delayed product launches and a petition to restore the old app; CEO Patrick Spence departed in January 2025.
business_impact: CEO departed January 2025; $20-30 million remediation; layoffs; sales decline

description: After a three-week online campaign led by activist Robby Starbuck, Tractor Supply announced it was eliminating its DEI roles, carbon-emission goals and Pride sponsorships.
reaction: Conservative activists claimed victory while the National Black Farmers Association called for the CEO's resignation and LGBTQ groups urged a boycott; the retreat set off a wave of corporate DEI rollbacks.
business_impact: criticism from both sides; no measurable sales impact; template for later rollbacks

description: A faulty CrowdStrike software update crashed about 8.5 million Windows computers worldwide, grounding flights, disrupting hospitals and halting businesses.
reaction: Global outrage at the largest IT outage in history, mockery of the company's $10 apology gift cards, a Delta lawsuit, and a House hearing where an executive apologized.
business_impact: stock fell more than 30%; Delta lawsuit; congressional hearing

description: Boar's Head expanded a listeria recall to more than 7 million pounds of deli meat as an outbreak linked to its Virginia plant grew to 10 deaths.
reaction: Public disgust intensified when USDA inspection records showing mold, insects and dripping liquid went viral; the company closed the plant indefinitely in September.
business_impact: plant closed; liverwurst discontinued; lawsuits; congressional inquiry

description: Harley-Davidson announced it had dropped DEI initiatives and quotas after an online pressure campaign by Robby Starbuck.
reaction: Conservative activists celebrated while LGBTQ groups and some dealers and riders criticized the retreat; the episode joined John Deere and Tractor Supply in a wave of rollbacks.
business_impact: criticism from both sides; no measurable sales impact

description: The CDC linked a deadly E. coli outbreak to McDonald's Quarter Pounders, later traced to slivered onions from a supplier.
reaction: National coverage, a stock drop of about 6%, and customer avoidance; McDonald's pulled the item in affected states and pledged $100 million to win back customers.
business_impact: stock down 6%; traffic declines; $100 million recovery spending

description: Owner Jeff Bezos blocked the Washington Post's planned presidential endorsement of Kamala Harris days before the election.
reaction: More than 250,000 readers cancelled subscriptions within days, editorial board members resigned, and staff publicly protested.
business_impact: about 10% of digital subscribers cancelled; editorial resignations

description: Jaguar unveiled a 'Copy Nothing' rebrand with a new logo and a teaser ad featuring avant-garde models and no cars.
reaction: Global viral ridicule, with Elon Musk asking 'Do you sell cars?', accusations of 'woke' branding, and the managing director condemning 'vile hatred' in responses.
business_impact: widespread brand mockery; rebrand executive departed in 2025 amid sales plunge during model changeover

description: Walmart, the largest US employer, announced it was rolling back DEI programs, ending racial equity training and leaving the Human Rights Campaign's index.
reaction: Civil rights and LGBTQ groups condemned the move and some customers pledged to shop elsewhere, while conservative activists claimed a major victory.
business_impact: criticism from left; no measurable sales impact

description: UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson was shot and killed in Manhattan, and the killing unleashed a wave of public anger at health insurers over denied claims.
reaction: Social media filled with stories of denied coverage and hostility toward insurers, the suspect drew online sympathy, and the company's CEO wrote an op-ed acknowledging public frustration.
business_impact: UnitedHealth stock fell sharply in following weeks; industry-wide scrutiny of claim denials

description: Anthem planned to stop paying for anesthesia beyond set time limits for surgeries in several states.
reaction: Anesthesiologists, patients and state officials denounced the policy in a viral wave amplified by anger at insurers; Anthem reversed it on December 5.
business_impact: policy reversed within days

description: Mark Zuckerberg announced Meta would end third-party fact-checking in the US, loosen hate-speech rules and move trust-and-safety teams to Texas.
reaction: Employees criticized the changes internally, fact-checking organizations and civil rights groups condemned them, and users publicized leaving for rival platforms.
business_impact: reputational; surge in account-deletion searches; no measurable revenue impact

description: Target announced it was ending its DEI goals and programs, reversing commitments made after 2020.
reaction: Black church leaders and activists launched boycotts including a 40-day 'Target Fast', foot traffic fell for months, and the company cited the backlash for weak sales.
business_impact: comparable sales declined for multiple quarters; CEO Brian Cornell announced departure August 2025; boycott formally ended March 2026

description: Jeff Bezos announced the Post's opinion section would advocate for 'personal liberties and free markets' and not publish opposing views, prompting the opinion editor's resignation.
reaction: Another wave of subscription cancellations, reported at more than 75,000 in 48 hours, and public criticism from current and former staff.
business_impact: tens of thousands of cancellations; opinion editor resigned

description: The 'Tesla Takedown' movement, which began in February 2025 in protest of Elon Musk's role leading DOGE, spread to weekly demonstrations at Tesla showrooms nationwide.
reaction: Hundreds of protests at dealerships, vandalism and arson at some sites, owners selling cars, and a global day of action on March 29.
business_impact: Q1 2025 deliveries down 13%; brand favorability collapsed; stock fell about 40% from December peak

description: Southwest ended its 50-year 'bags fly free' policy and announced other fee changes under pressure from activist investor Elliott.
reaction: Loyal customers flooded social media with anger and vows to switch airlines; the decision became a symbol of the airline abandoning its identity.
business_impact: customer anger; company later reported bag-fee revenue above expectations

description: Budget carrier Avelo signed a contract to operate deportation flights for ICE from Mesa, Arizona.
reaction: Protests at its New Haven and West Coast bases, a boycott petition with more than 30,000 signatures, and calls from Connecticut officials to cancel the contract.
business_impact: boycott petitions and protests; company defended contract

description: CEO Luis von Ahn announced Duolingo would be 'AI-first' and gradually stop using contractors for work AI could do.
reaction: Users posted screenshots of deleting the app, the brand's social accounts went dark and later mocked the uproar, and von Ahn walked back the framing.
business_impact: brand backlash; CEO clarification; no measurable user loss

description: Walmart warned on its earnings call that it would raise prices because of tariffs.
reaction: President Trump publicly told Walmart to 'eat the tariffs' and stop blaming his policy, and shoppers debated the retailer's pricing on social media.
business_impact: presidential criticism; company reiterated it would keep prices as low as possible

description: Federal immigration agents conducted raids targeting day laborers in Home Depot parking lots in Los Angeles, and the company declined to intervene or comment substantively.
reaction: Protests at stores, calls for a boycott over the company's perceived cooperation, and later a holiday-season 'We Ain't Buying It' boycott campaign.
business_impact: boycott campaigns; no measurable sales impact reported

description: Paramount agreed to pay $16 million to settle President Trump's lawsuit over a '60 Minutes' interview while seeking federal approval for its Skydance merger.
reaction: Senators called the settlement 'bribery in plain sight', press-freedom groups condemned it, and CBS's own host Stephen Colbert mocked it on air.
business_impact: reputational; preceded Colbert cancellation and talent departures

description: Elon Musk's Grok chatbot posted antisemitic content, praised Hitler and called itself 'MechaHitler' after a prompt update.
reaction: Widespread condemnation from the ADL and users, posts were deleted, xAI apologized, and X CEO Linda Yaccarino resigned the next day.
business_impact: X CEO resigned; xAI apology; several countries restricted Grok

description: A Coldplay concert 'kiss cam' caught Astronomer CEO Andy Byron embracing the company's HR chief, and the clip went globally viral.
reaction: Hundreds of millions of views, memes and intense scrutiny of the company; Byron resigned on July 19 and the HR executive followed.
business_impact: CEO resigned; HR chief resigned

description: CBS announced it would cancel 'The Late Show with Stephen Colbert' in May 2026, days after Colbert criticized Paramount's settlement with Trump.
reaction: Fans, fellow hosts and Democratic senators accused the company of a politically motivated cancellation and called for boycotts; Trump celebrated the decision.
business_impact: reputational; senators demanded answers; no direct financial impact

description: Delta said it was expanding AI-assisted pricing to about 20% of domestic fares, which critics interpreted as individualized 'surveillance pricing'.
reaction: Senators demanded answers, consumer advocates and travelers voiced outrage online, and Delta issued a statement denying it would use personal data to set fares.
business_impact: clarification issued; senators' inquiry

description: American Eagle's 'Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans' campaign played on 'jeans/genes', which critics read as a eugenics-tinged message.
reaction: Viral criticism from the left and enthusiastic defense from the right including President Trump; the company stood by the campaign and its stock jumped.
business_impact: stock rose more than 20%; brand awareness surged; no apology

description: Reuters reported internal Meta guidelines had permitted AI chatbots to engage in 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children.
reaction: Senator Hawley opened an investigation, dozens of state attorneys general sent warnings, and the company revised its chatbot policies.
business_impact: Senate probe; policy changes; FTC inquiry into AI companions

description: Cracker Barrel unveiled a simplified logo that removed the 'old timer' figure and barrel as part of a modernization effort.
reaction: Conservative commentators and customers denounced the change as erasing heritage, the stock fell sharply, President Trump weighed in, and the company restored the old logo on August 26.
business_impact: market value fell roughly $100 million; logo reversed; CEO Julie Masino stepped down July 2026

description: ABC suspended 'Jimmy Kimmel Live!' indefinitely after FCC chair Brendan Carr criticized Kimmel's remarks about the Charlie Kirk assassination and affiliates Nexstar and Sinclair pulled the show.
reaction: Backlash from the left over censorship and from the right over Kimmel's comments; Disney+ and Hulu cancellations surged and celebrities urged boycotts before Kimmel returned September 23.
business_impact: reported 1.7 million streaming cancellations; stock dipped; show reinstated within a week

description: The NFL announced Puerto Rican artist Bad Bunny, a critic of ICE who performs mostly in Spanish, as the Super Bowl LX halftime headliner.
reaction: Conservative figures and President Trump denounced the choice and Turning Point USA announced a rival 'All-American Halftime Show', while supporters celebrated; the debate ran until the February 2026 game.
business_impact: no measurable impact; rival halftime show staged by Turning Point USA

description: CEO Marc Benioff told the New York Times he would welcome National Guard troops in San Francisco ahead of Dreamforce.
reaction: Local officials, tech leaders and employees criticized him, investor Ron Conway resigned from his foundation board, and Benioff apologized a week later.
business_impact: CEO apology; board resignation at foundation

description: Amazon announced 14,000 corporate layoffs, the largest in its history, as it poured capital into AI.
reaction: Public debate over AI replacing white-collar work, criticism from lawmakers and employees, and viral accounts of abrupt notifications.
business_impact: 14,000 jobs cut; second round of 16,000 followed in January 2026

company: Tyson Foods / JBS / Cargill / National Beef
description: With retail beef prices at record highs, President Trump ordered a Justice Department investigation into the four dominant meatpackers for alleged price fixing.
reaction: Consumer anger over grocery prices and bipartisan calls to break up meatpacker concentration, with ranchers and consumer groups backing the probe.
business_impact: DOJ and USDA investigation

description: Unionized Starbucks baristas launched an open-ended 'Red Cup Rebellion' strike on the chain's busiest promotional day over stalled contract talks.
reaction: Strikes spread to more than 100 cities, politicians and celebrities voiced support, and customers were urged to boycott until a contract was reached.
business_impact: strike spread to hundreds of stores; sustained pressure through holiday season

description: CBS News under editor-in-chief Bari Weiss pulled a completed '60 Minutes' report on El Salvador's CECOT prison hours before air, citing a need for 'additional reporting'.
reaction: Correspondents and liberal critics accused the network of spiking a story unfavorable to the Trump administration, the segment leaked, and CBS aired it on January 18 after sustained backlash.
business_impact: segment aired after delay; reputational damage to CBS News

description: After weeks of reports that Grok on X was generating sexualized 'bikini' images of real people, including in some cases children, from ordinary photos without consent, X issued a statement on January 3 placing responsibility on users who prompt it.
reaction: Global outrage, temporary bans in Indonesia and Malaysia, a UK Ofcom investigation, a California attorney general cease-and-desist order, class-action suits, and X restricting the feature in mid-January.
business_impact: feature restricted; multiple government investigations; class actions

description: As a federal immigration surge in Minnesota escalated, with two people fatally shot by agents and Target employees detained, hundreds of Target workers wrote to the CEO criticizing the company's 'continued inaction' and hundreds of local businesses closed in a one-day general strike.
reaction: Public criticism of corporate silence from employees and activists; on January 25 more than 60 Minnesota CEOs including Target's, Best Buy's and General Mills' signed a letter calling for 'de-escalation' that critics said avoided naming ICE or the victims.
business_impact: joint corporate statement; local sales drops of 40-80% reported by Minneapolis business leaders

description: Days after the Oracle-led US joint venture took control of TikTok, users reported outages and alleged suppression of content about ICE and the Epstein files.
reaction: #DeleteTikTok trended, Democratic lawmakers demanded answers, and California's attorney general opened an investigation; the company blamed a data-center issue.
business_impact: California AG investigation; user exodus claims; company denial

description: Amazon confirmed a second round of 16,000 corporate layoffs, after some employees learned of the cuts through an email sent in error.
reaction: Criticism of the botched communication and renewed public anxiety about AI-driven white-collar job losses.
business_impact: 16,000 jobs cut; about 30,000 total since October 2025

description: A Waymo robotaxi struck a child near a Santa Monica elementary school, and NHTSA opened a federal investigation.
reaction: Public alarm about driverless cars near schools, calls from local officials to pause operations, and renewed scrutiny after earlier school-bus incidents.
business_impact: NHTSA investigation; local calls for restrictions

description: Mark Zuckerberg testified in a landmark Los Angeles trial alleging Meta and YouTube deliberately designed addictive products that harmed a young plaintiff.
reaction: Intense national coverage of internal documents and testimony, parent-advocacy campaigns, and on March 25 a jury found both companies liable and awarded $6 million.
business_impact: jury verdict against Meta and YouTube; thousands of similar cases pending

description: Block cut about 4,000 jobs, nearly half its workforce, with CEO Jack Dorsey citing AI and warning other companies would follow.
reaction: Backlash from employees and the public over the scale and framing, with Dorsey's comments becoming a flashpoint in the debate over AI job losses.
business_impact: about 4,000 jobs cut; stock rose on the news

description: Meta laid off about 8,000 employees, roughly 10% of its workforce, to fund AI investment, with Zuckerberg warning that AI success 'isn't a given'.
reaction: Public and employee anger over profitable companies cutting jobs for AI, adding to a wave of 2026 tech layoffs that drew political attention.
business_impact: about 8,000 jobs cut

description: Pepsi posted on Threads that 'Pepsi Wild Cherry is what happens when regular cherry stops asking permission'.
reaction: Users read the line as a joke about sexual consent; the post was deleted within hours and Pepsi apologized.
business_impact: post deleted, apology, no lasting impact

company: Good Good Golf / Callaway (Topgolf Callaway Brands)
description: A co-branded driver ad from golf media company Good Good and Callaway showed a man shoving a woman to the ground when she reached for the club, framed as a horror-film parody.
reaction: Viral condemnation as glorifying violence against women and calls to boycott Callaway; Callaway apologized and cut ties, retailers pulled Good Good merchandise, and Good Good's CEO and president were out by September 2.
business_impact: CEO and president departed; Callaway ended partnership; Dick's and Golf Galaxy pulled merchandise; Golf Channel series cancelled

description: Sports-betting exchange Novig released a 'Just Sports' campaign featuring Sydney Sweeney unclothed and covered only by sports equipment.
reaction: Prominent female athletes condemned the ad as sexualizing women's sports and the criticism went viral; the company's CEO defended it as forcing Novig into the national conversation.
business_impact: no retraction; brand awareness gain alongside athlete criticism

description: A Converse ad featuring K-pop star Karina showed a spotlight shape on her skirt that viewers said resembled a KKK hood, alongside imagery compared to lynching.
reaction: Widespread condemnation on social media; Converse pulled the ad and apologized for 'deeply upsetting' imagery.
business_impact: ad pulled, apology
